notes: Author of The Colony: Stories from a Down East Island (2016) and son of Lowell Pierson Beveridge Sr. and Ida Gattrell Beveridge. In a May 23, 2012 Brooklyn Historical Society interview, he remembers opposition from some extended relatives to his January 1954 marriage to Hortense 'Tee' Sie, his resulting feeling of being unwelcome at North Haven for roughly 20 years, and subsequent renewed family visits. He explicitly says his own parents eventually supported the marriage. This is his personal recollection; do not label every family member an objector or claim a formal legal banishment. No independently verified death record located as of this review; protect contemporary personal details and do not expose exact birth date.
evidence_status: Identity, parentage and book authorship strongly supported by 1991 obituary, self-identification in 2012 interview and 2016 family memoir. Family responses attributed to narrator; independently uncorroborated.

notes: Film editor and documentary filmmaker whose pioneering career is documented in scholarly film-history research. Her husband Pete Beveridge says in a first-person May 2012 interview that they married at St. Philip's Church in Harlem in January 1954 (NOT in 1953). Their relationship and early civil-rights work faced objections from some extended family members; this statement is attributable to his own recollection rather than an inference about the beliefs of every relative.
evidence_status: 1954 marriage and relationship reported by husband in archived firsthand oral history; film work separately documented in Duke University Press study. Birth/death years reported in secondary film history and require vital-record corroboration.
